note: **Block-local variables are decided lexically, and the model decides them dynamically.** A Proc/lambda body assigning a name that becomes an outer local only *later in the text* writes the outer local here; in Ruby the block's `a` is block-local, because at the point the block was written no `a` existed. Pre-existing and unrelated to the L123 coerce work it was found alongside (confirmed by `git stash` + rebuild on this same repro). Characterized: an `each` block in the same shape **agrees**, by accident of timing — it runs before the outer assignment, so no slot exists yet — and only a stored-and-called-later Proc separates the two rules. The fix starts in the desugarer: the exported AST is `["block", params, [], body]`, with nowhere to record which assignment targets were new at parse time. Found by a tier-1 campaign that ran *concurrently* with another tier-1 campaign which drew all 250 programs and reported 0 disagreements (N42). **Fixed in C35/L125**: Prism computes the parse-time local set per scope, and the block node gained a fourth slot (`declared`) to carry it; the Lean decoder merges it with the explicit `|;x|` list, which the block frame already seeds as nil — so the assignment resolves in the block's own frame. The tier reported this case `unexpectedly_fixed` before the sidecar was flipped, which is N41's second direction firing as designed.
